title: Antipodal Symmetry Kills the Door-Graph Endpoint Parity — a No-Go Theorem for Tucker Levels
description: The door-counting program for Tucker's lemma reduces the full-dimensional theorem to one open input — the geometric bridge that identifies the boundary doors of the dimension-(n+1) complex with the interior complementary simplices of the dimension-n complex — and consumes an ODD interior-endpoint count of the almost-complementary door graph at each level. The sibling entry sperner-mathlib4-oq-02-oq-01 found empirically that the natural door graph can be entirely empty of endpoints while Tucker still holds, concluding that the remaining input must be an oriented / antipodally-signed count, not any door-counting parity. This entry proves the dimension-free structural reason, entirely by finite-combinatorial means (0 axioms, no decide). Let σ be the antipodal map on the top cells of a door graph G with boundary predicate B. If σ is a free involution (no cell is its own antipode) that is also a boundary-preserving graph automorphism, then σ pairs the degree-1 endpoints into antipodal 2-orbits, forcing BOTH the interior and the boundary endpoint counts to be EVEN. But a Tucker level requires the interior count ODD (this is exactly what the verified TuckerTower.tower_interior_odd propagates and what exists_interior_of_odd turns into a complementary simplex). The two are contradictory: symmetric_graph_not_tucker_level shows an antipodally-symmetric door graph can never be a Tucker level. Hence the odd count can appear only once the symmetry is BROKEN — on a hemisphere fundamental domain, where σ swaps the two hemispheres and ceases to be an automorphism. The labelling-induced asymmetry of the almost-complementary door graph is therefore essential, not incidental, and this is the abstract obstruction that pins the exact shape of the open bridge. The general lemma even_card_filter_of_free_involution (a free involution preserving a decidable predicate forces an even fibre) is reusable Mathlib-gap infrastructure.

overview.historicalContext: Tucker's lemma (Albert W. Tucker, 1945) is the combinatorial heart of the Borsuk–Ulam theorem. Its constructive proofs (Freund–Todd 1981; Prescott–Su 2005) build a graph of maximum degree ≤ 2 on the almost-complementary simplices whose interior degree-1 vertices are exactly the complementary simplices Tucker asserts, and follow a path from a forced boundary endpoint to an interior one. The grandparent entry sperner-mathlib4 verifies the abstract door-counting engine and its dimension recursion (TuckerTower), leaving a single geometric bridge as the open obligation. The sibling entries sperner-mathlib4-oq-02 and sperner-mathlib4-oq-02-oq-01 established, on the concrete hexagon triangulation of B², that no UNSIGNED door count supplies the odd boundary seed the engine needs, and conjectured the input must be an oriented / antipodally-signed count. This entry supplies the dimension-free structural theorem behind that empirical finding.
overview.problemStatement: Fix a finite door graph G on the top cells (the almost-complementary simplices), a decidable boundary predicate B, and the antipodal map σ. The tower's interiorEndpoints G B = {v | G.degree v = 1 ∧ ¬ B v} and boundaryEndpoints G B = {v | G.degree v = 1 ∧ B v} are the degree-1 vertices; the induction consumes Odd (#interiorEndpoints) at each level. Suppose σ is (i) a free involution: σ (σ v) = v and σ v ≠ v for all v; (ii) a graph automorphism: G.Adj (σ v) (σ w) ↔ G.Adj v w; (iii) boundary-preserving: B (σ v) ↔ B v. Prove that under these hypotheses both #interiorEndpoints and #boundaryEndpoints are even, hence the interior count is never odd, hence no such antipodally-symmetric door graph can serve as a Tucker level (which requires an odd interior count).
overview.proofStrategy: The argument is elementary finite combinatorics, 0 axioms and no decide. First, a free involution forces even cardinality (even_card_of_free_involution): sum the constant 1 over ZMod 2 and cancel antipodal pairs via Finset.sum_ninvolution. Second, this transfers to any σ-invariant decidable predicate P by restricting σ to the subtype {a // P a}, on which it is still a free involution, giving even_card_filter_of_free_involution: Even #{a | P a}. Third, a graph automorphism preserves degree (degree_eq_of_aut) because σ maps the neighbour finset of σ v bijectively onto that of v (a Finset.card_bij with witness σ). The interior/boundary endpoint predicates G.degree v = 1 ∧ (¬)B v are σ-invariant — degree by degree_eq_of_aut, boundary by hypothesis (iii) — so even_card_filter_of_free_involution applies and both counts are even (even_card_interiorEndpoints, even_card_boundaryEndpoints). Finally not_odd_card_interiorEndpoints and symmetric_graph_not_tucker_level contradict the tower's odd-interior requirement.
keyInsights: The object the Tucker induction actually consumes is not the raw boundary-door set (already known even, by SpernerTuckerAntipodalParity.even_card_antipodal_boundary) but the degree-1 ENDPOINTS of the almost-complementary door graph. This entry proves the analogue for that object: under an honest antipodal symmetry the endpoints split into free 2-orbits, so their count is even.

The parity obstruction is dimension-free and structural, not a coincidence of any particular triangulation. Whenever the antipodal involution is a boundary-preserving graph automorphism, the interior endpoint count is forced even — so Tucker's odd interior count, which the verified TuckerTower.tower_interior_odd propagates, is unreachable.

This explains WHY the geometric bridge is hard and pins its exact shape: the odd count can only appear once the antipodal symmetry is broken. Passing to a hemisphere fundamental domain (SpernerTuckerHemisphere.card_eq_two_mul_hemisphere) does exactly that — σ maps one hemisphere to the other and is no longer an automorphism — so the labelling-induced asymmetry of the door graph is essential, not incidental.

The engine of the proof, even_card_filter_of_free_involution (a free involution preserving a decidable predicate forces an even fibre), is a reusable Mathlib-gap lemma: it upgrades the p-group-flavoured card_modEq_card_fixedPoints to the elementary free-involution setting and restricts it to an arbitrary invariant predicate.

sections.title: A Free Involution Forces an Even Fibre
sections.summary: Reproves even_card_of_free_involution (a fixed-point-free involution has even domain cardinality, via summing 1 over ZMod 2 and cancelling antipodal pairs with Finset.sum_ninvolution) and upgrades it to even_card_filter_of_free_involution: if σ is a free involution and the decidable predicate P is σ-invariant, then #{a | P a} is even. The upgrade transports the base fact along the subtype {a // P a}, on which σ restricts to a free involution.

sections.title: Antipodal Symmetry Preserves Degree
sections.summary: Sets up the antipodal symmetry data: a door graph G, boundary predicate B, and involution σ. degree_eq_of_aut shows that a graph automorphism preserves the degree of every vertex — σ carries the neighbour finset of σ v bijectively onto that of v (a Finset.card_bij with witness map σ, using the involution and automorphism hypotheses).

sections.title: Even Endpoint Counts Under Symmetry
sections.summary: The interior-endpoint predicate G.degree v = 1 ∧ ¬ B v and the boundary-endpoint predicate G.degree v = 1 ∧ B v are σ-invariant (degree by degree_eq_of_aut, boundary membership by hypothesis), so even_card_filter_of_free_involution applies: even_card_interiorEndpoints and even_card_boundaryEndpoints give even counts, and not_odd_card_interiorEndpoints records that the interior count is therefore never odd.

sections.title: The No-Go Theorem for Tucker Levels
sections.summary: symmetric_graph_not_tucker_level: a free, automorphic, boundary-preserving antipodal involution together with an ODD interior-endpoint count is contradictory. Since the verified TuckerTower.tower_interior_odd forces an odd interior count at every Tucker level, an antipodally-symmetric door graph can never be a Tucker level — the odd count requires the symmetry to be broken (a hemisphere fundamental domain).

conclusion.summary: Working dimension-free over an arbitrary finite door graph with a boundary predicate and an antipodal involution, and using only elementary finite combinatorics (0 axioms, no decide), the entry proves that if the antipodal map is a free involution AND a boundary-preserving graph automorphism, then both the interior and the boundary degree-1 endpoint counts are even. The verified Tucker dimension recursion requires an ODD interior count at every level, so an antipodally-symmetric door graph can never be a Tucker level. Seven theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: This is the dimension-free structural reason behind the sibling entries' empirical finding that no unsigned door count fires the engine. The odd interior-endpoint count Tucker needs is unreachable while the antipodal symmetry is intact; it can appear only after the symmetry is broken by passing to a hemisphere fundamental domain, where σ swaps the two hemispheres and is no longer an automorphism. So the labelling-induced asymmetry of the almost-complementary door graph is essential, and the open geometric bridge must be built on the hemisphere, drawing its oddness from the lower-dimensional (equatorial) Tucker instance — exactly the shape the hemisphere reduction (card_eq_two_mul_hemisphere) prepares.
openQuestions: Construct the antipodal graph automorphism explicitly on a concrete B^{n+1} triangulation and verify that its restriction to a hemisphere fundamental domain breaks the automorphism property in precisely the way that reintroduces an odd interior-endpoint count.

Combine this no-go theorem with SpernerTuckerHemisphere.card_eq_two_mul_hemisphere to reduce the open bridge to an equality between hemisphere boundary endpoints and level-n interior simplices, completing the TuckerTower.bridge input.
